issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Coach-chat output safety filter SUPPRESSES the mandated crisis/self-harm referral (validate_output Layer 4 over-match). Route: /coach-chat.

WHAT IS WRONG: In the live coach pipeline (nyu_backend/llm_service.py get_coach_response -> validate_output, lines 320-326) Layer 4 runs _harmful_health_regex over the COACH RESPONSE. That regex includes (?:self[- ]?harm|suicid) (line 111). When a user is in crisis and the coach replies -- per its own SOP (llm_prompts.py:905 "For self-harm/eating disorder: surface iCall (9152987821) and Vandrevala Foundation (1860-2662-345) by name"; llm_prompts.py:94) -- with an empathetic message that names "suicide"/"self-harm" and those helplines, validate_output matches the words, DISCARDS the whole response, and returns the generic deflection (line 326): "I want to make sure I give you safe advice. For this topic, I would recommend consulting with a healthcare professional. Can I help you with something else?" (passed=False). get_coach_response returns that string (line 1288) to the user.

EXPECTED: user disclosing suicidal ideation gets the empathetic RED-tier response WITH iCall + Vandrevala numbers by name.
ACTUAL: most-vulnerable user gets a dismissive deflection, NO helpline numbers, ending "Can I help you with something else?". The filter meant to stop the LLM ADVOCATING self-harm over-matches any mention -- including the protective referral the system is REQUIRED to give.

REPRO (backend code trace):
1. /coach-chat, user: "I keep having thoughts of suicide / hurting myself."
2. LLM (per llm_prompts.py:905/94) returns a caring reply containing "suicide"/"self-harm" + the two helpline numbers.
3. llm_service.py:321 _harmful_health_regex.search(response) matches -> line 326 returns the deflection, replacing the real answer (returned at :1288).
Net: crisis referral gagged on the live coach path. (First PHQ-9 prefill "...took the PHQ-9...would like to talk" passes; the follow-up crisis turn is where it triggers.)

SECONDARY (same root): Layer 4 also gags legitimate eating-disorder referrals that name "purging"/"laxative abuse" (HARMFUL_HEALTH_PATTERNS line 109) or "starvation diet" (line 106) -- any coach reply naming the behaviour to refer the user is replaced.

FIX: make Layer 4 context-aware for protective/referral content -- exempt responses that contain the helpline numbers/referral phrasing, or drop self-harm|suicid from the OUTPUT harmful-advice regex (it belongs to input-intent detection, not to gating the coach caring reply). Files: llm_service.py:104-113 (HARMFUL_HEALTH_PATTERNS), :320-326 (validate_output Layer 4), :1269 (call site); contract in llm_prompts.py:94,905.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Achievements "Active Streaks" card never renders — GET /gamification/overview streaks block is fed by dead GamificationProfile counters.

get_gamification_overview() (nyu_backend/app/services/gamification_service.py:599-607) sources streaks.tracking_days / workout_weeks / step_goal_days / checkin_days and longest_tracking / longest_workout from GamificationProfile.tracking_streak_days etc. Those columns are written ONLY inside gamification_service.process_streak(), which is UNWIRED — it has no production caller (the live streak engine daily_report._evaluate_streak writes FitnessPlan.current_streak instead; checkin_streak_days has no writer anywhere). So all four gate fields are permanently 0 in prod.

Achievements.tsx:116-119 gates the whole section on hasActiveStreaks = tracking_days>0 || workout_weeks>0 || step_goal_days>0 || checkin_days>0. Because those are always 0, the Active Streaks card — plus the live "N freezes left" sub-label and the Best-tracking/Best-workout line nested inside it — NEVER show, even for a user with a real multi-day streak.

Expected: a user with an active streak (visible on the dashboard / GET /gamification/streak, which reads FitnessPlan.current_streak) sees that streak on /achievements.
Actual: the Active Streaks section is absent for every user.

Repro: (1) log daily so FitnessPlan.current_streak >= 1; (2) GET /api/v1/gamification/streak returns current_streak>0 while GET /api/v1/gamification/overview returns streaks.tracking_days=0; (3) open /achievements — no Active Streaks card.

Fix: in get_gamification_overview() source tracking_days/longest from FitnessPlan.current_streak/longest_streak (mirror the /gamification/streak route + backend.py:3701), or wire process_streak() into the nightly pipeline. freeze_available (line 606) is already live — only the count fields are dead.

So with BOTH fixes, a user who builds a compliant streak (day_score>=0.75) will see the Active-Streaks card render on /achievements.

Remaining dead fields (workout_weeks / step_goal_days / checkin_days) still have no live writer — those stay 0 until process_streak() is wired into the nightly pipeline (a larger, separate task). tracking_days (the primary card gate) is now live. To close: click Resolve.

issues.description: [suggestion] Quick re-log a past meal ("Log again") on the Nutrition screen. Problem: Indian daily eating is repetitive (same roti-dal-sabzi, same protein shake) but every entry today requires re-typing/re-searching the meal from scratch (or photo/barcode) even when it was logged yesterday or last week. Evidence: repo has no copy-previous-meal/quick-repeat action (grepped NutritionMealCard, CustomMealModal, meal-log flow — only diet-plan-builder has an unrelated "repeat" match for weekly plan structure, not daily logging); comparable trackers (MyFitnessPal "Copy from previous day", Cronometer favorites) ship this as a core retention lever. v1 scope: add a "Log again" action on past meal-history entries (NutritionMealCard / meal detail) that duplicates the stored meal_name + macros + quantity into a new log row for today at the tapped meal slot, no AI/recompute needed since macros are already persisted. No new screen, no favorites list yet (that would be v2). Effort: ~1-2 days FE (action + duplicate-log API call) + confirm backend already exposes a create-meal-log endpoint that accepts prefilled macros (likely yes, reused by manual entry).

issues.description: [suggestion] Voice/text meal logging: speak or type what you ate in your own words and let the coach AI parse it into a food entry, instead of only manual fields or a photo. USER PROBLEM: Add Custom Meal (src/components/nutrition/CustomMealModal.tsx) only takes manual name/calories/macro fields today -- no free-text or voice path exists (grepped: no parse/describe/freeform handling in that modal, no SpeechRecognition usage anywhere in src). Snap-to-log (photo, i-20260706-sn4p) covers the visual case but not hands-busy moments (cooking, eating out, driving) or dishes that photograph poorly (mixed thali, soup, chai+snack). Competitors (MyFitnessPal voice log, Cal AI) ship this; NYUS has neither text-freeform nor voice entry. EVIDENCE: backend already has an LLM meal-estimation path for the photo flow (llm_service.py) -- the same prompt pattern (food description -> structured items+macros) can be reused for a transcript/typed string, so this is largely a UI + one new endpoint, not new AI infra. Also ties into the in-flight i18n directive: Hindi/Hinglish speech-to-text + parsing is a natural differentiator for the India-focused base. V1 SCOPE: in the Add Custom Meal sheet, add a "Describe it" text field (mic button using the Web Speech API on web / native STT on Capacitor where available, falling back to typed text) -> POST the transcript to a new /api/v1/nutrition/parse-meal-text endpoint -> LLM returns items+macros -> prefill the existing manual fields, editable before save (same edit-then-confirm pattern already used for photo logging). No new logging surfaces, no schema changes to DailyLog. EFFORT: ~1-2 days FE (mic capture + prefill wiring reusing existing food-item form) + ~0.5 day BE (one endpoint, reuse llm_service prompt scaffolding).
